desc:
The marbles weights[0..n-1] lie in a row. You must split the row into exactly k non-empty bags, each bag being a block of consecutive marbles. The cost of a bag that spans indices i..j is weights[i] + weights[j] (for a bag with a single marble that is twice its weight). The score of a split is the sum of the costs of its bags.

Over all valid splits, find the maximum score and the minimum score, and return maximum minus minimum.

weights = [1, 3, 5, 1], k = 2   -> 4
weights = [1, 3], k = 2         -> 0
weights = [4, 2, 9], k = 1      -> 0

In the first example the splits [1][3,5,1], [1,3][5,1], [1,3,5][1] score 6, 10 and 8, so the answer is 10 - 6.
hints: Write the score of a split in terms of its cut points. Every split always includes the first and the last marble in its cost; what else is counted?
Each cut between positions i and i+1 adds weights[i] + weights[i+1] to the score, on top of the fixed weights[0] + weights[n-1]. The k - 1 cuts are independent of each other.

Compute the n - 1 values weights[i] + weights[i+1] and sort them. The maximum score takes the k - 1 largest of them, the minimum score takes the k - 1 smallest; the fixed part cancels in the difference.
editorial: Consider a split with cuts after positions c_1 < c_2 < … < c_{k-1}. The bags are [0..c_1], [c_1+1..c_2], …. The first bag contributes weights[0] + weights[c_1], the next one weights[c_1+1] + weights[c_2], and so on. Grouping the terms, the score equals weights[0] + weights[n-1] + ∑ (weights[c] + weights[c+1]) over the cuts.

So the score is a constant plus the sum of the pair values pair[c] = weights[c] + weights[c+1] of the chosen cuts, and any set of k - 1 distinct cut positions among the n - 1 gaps is a valid split. Hence the maximum score uses the k - 1 largest pair values and the minimum uses the k - 1 smallest. The constant cancels when subtracting.
Sort the pair values and subtract the sum of the k - 1 smallest from the sum of the k - 1 largest. When k = 1 or k = n the two sets coincide and the answer is 0. Time O(n log n).
